claims.claim: Operating a node, validating transactions, providing a read-only blockchain interface, developing or distributing open-source blockchain or DeFi protocol software, operating non-custodial wallets, and participating in liquidity pools are all exempt from SEC registration
claims.sourceSpan: (4) Developing, publishing, constituting, administering, maintaining, or otherwise distributing a blockchain system or a decentralized finance trading protocol. ... (6) Developing, publishing, constituting, administering, maintaining, or otherwise distributing software or systems that create or deploy hardware or software, including wallets or other systems, facilitating an individual user's own personal ability to keep, safeguard, or custody the user's digital assets
claims.section: Bill Title III / new Section 15H (Sec 15H(4) and (6))
claims.note: QA Pass 3 (2026-08-12): Sec 15H(4) does NOT restrict its exemption to "open-source" — that qualifier is invented (the phrase "open source" appears in the bill only at line 2410 inside Sec 205 maturity criteria, not as a limiter on the Sec 15H(4) exemption). Sec 15H(6) exempts the developing/distributing of wallet SOFTWARE, not the end-user act of "operating non-custodial wallets" — different actor/activity. Fixed by aligning the top_lines gloss to the source categories: operating a node/oracle service, read-only user-interface, developing/distributing blockchain/DeFi protocol, operating/participating in a liquidity pool, and developing/distributing non-custodial wallet software.

claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 105. Rulemakings. ... SEC. 105. RULEMAKINGS. ... (c) Protection of Self-Custody.--
claims.note: QA Pass 3 (2026-08-12): Section 105 is titled "Rulemakings" (bill TOC L40, section heading L1055). Protection of Self-Custody is subsection (c) inside Sec 105 (L1085). There is also a separate SEC. 22 PROTECTION OF SELF-CUSTODY at L5721 inside a securities-law amendment. Fixed the section label to "Section 105(c) — Protection of Self-Custody".

claims.claim: Directs the CFTC and SEC to conduct studies on decentralized finance, non-fungible tokens, financial literacy, market infrastructure, blockchain in payments, illicit use of digital assets, foreign adversary intermediaries, and foreign adversary participation
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 504. STUDY ON DECENTRALIZED FINANCE. [L5215] ... SEC. 505. STUDY ON NON-FUNGIBLE TOKENS. [L5311, Comptroller General-led] ... SEC. 506. STUDY ON EXPANDING FINANCIAL LITERACY AMONGST DIGITAL [COMMODITY HOLDERS] [L5353] ... SEC. 507. STUDY ON FINANCIAL MARKET INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS. [L5400] ... SEC. 508. STUDY ON BLOCKCHAIN IN PAYMENTS. [L5424, Treasury-led] ... SEC. 509. STUDY ON ILLICIT USE OF DIGITAL ASSETS. [L5442, Treasury-led, in consultation with CFTC/SEC] ... SEC. 510. GAO STUDY ON CERTAIN CENTRALIZED INTERMEDIARIES THAT ARE [primarily foreign] [L5464, GAO-led] ... SEC. 511. STUDIES ON FOREIGN ADVERSARY PARTICIPATION. [L5482, Treasury-led (a) + GAO leg (b)]
claims.note: QA Pass 4 (2026-08-12): analysis attributed ALL Title V studies to "the CFTC and SEC" but the section headings show mixed conductors — Sec 505 is GAO-only (Comptroller General), Sec 510 is GAO-only, Secs 508/509/511(a) are Treasury-led, and Sec 511(b) is a separate GAO leg. Only Secs 504/506/507 are CFTC/SEC-led. Class-3 entity error (right facts, wrong actor). Fixed sections[4].items[1].main to enumerate the correct conductor per section, and rewrote the detail to quote the actual Sec 511(a) study elements (identify foreign-adversary-owned registrants; assess trading-data collection on U.S. persons; evaluate IP misuse/theft) instead of the previous unsourced "national security implications" gloss.
